state: Yes: a tax card, valid 1 May to 30 April and renewed yearly after filing returns and paying the tax due, is required for any financial, commercial or service contract, purchases, supplies, and for issuing or renewing a business licence; one card per taxpayer (تُعد البطاقة الضريبية من الوثائق األساسية التي تٌطلب)

condition: When a business must notify the tax administration that it has started trading
state: Within 30 days of starting, for income-tax payers; within 60 days of starting to let property; within 60 days for exempt small enterprises in the free professions (خالل:)

condition: What a business needs to obtain a tax number
state: A notice of starting activity (form 1) with copies of: the national electronic ID card (passport for non-Yemenis); lease or ownership proof for the premises, branches and stores; the commercial or industrial register; the activity licence; professional and other licences; for companies, the articles and memorandum; the premises are inspected on site to confirm they suit the activity; no service fee; done within 3 working days of a complete application (ال يوجد رسوم الخدمة)
note: First-time importers must also lodge a bank guarantee (YQ-B173).

condition: What guarantee a business must give the Tax Authority to import
state: An original cash bank guarantee at the central bank or one of its branches, or at a commercial bank it authorises with the central bank's endorsement, in favour of the Tax Authority for one year: from first-time importers, and from a registered taxpayer adding import activity (who must also settle any tax due); the amount for large and medium importers is set by decision of the head of the Authority (أصل خطاب ضما بنكي (نقد ))

condition: When a business must notify the tax administration of a new activity or changed data
state: Within 30 days of adding an activity or changing data, for income-tax payers; within 21 days of a change in sales-tax data, for those registered for sales tax (يوماً من تأريخ إضافة نشاط /تعديل بيانات)

condition: Whether a small business pays profits tax
state: No: small and micro enterprises are exempt from commercial and industrial profits tax, non-commercial profits tax, and wages tax on their workers (a small one: annual turnover above 1.5 million and up to 20 million rials, 4 to 9 workers); excepted are import, exchange and money transfer, supplies and contracting, gold and jewellery, doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, consultants, and foreign taxpayers (املنشآت الصغري واألصغر املعفا من ضريبة األرباح)
note: Under law 8 of 2020 amending income tax law 17 of 2010, as the guide states.

condition: What suspends a business's tax number
state: Automatic suspension through the tax-procedures system when the taxpayer does not file the annual income-tax return within a year after it is due, does not file sales-tax returns for three consecutive periods, or does not pay final tax due after the notice period; on stopping, assigning or liquidating the business; when the business is not found at its registered address; and, with the head of the Authority's approval, to protect public revenue or fight tax evasion (يتم تعليق الرقم الضريبي بشكل تلقائي)

condition: When a business can reclaim tax it paid
state: Within five years of paying (the right then lapses), only by the payer, any final tax due being set off first, keeping the invoices and records for those five years: income tax paid above the tax due, twice or without right (the applicant must hold an active tax number and file returns), refunded within 40 days of a complete request; sales tax, for registered persons, on goods exported as they are or to free zones, on inputs to exports, collected in error or paid twice, on input tax left at the year's end (for production inputs, whenever input tax exceeds output tax), on zero-rated baby milk and international transport services, refunded within a month; bodies exempt under art. 42 of the sales tax law (embassies, international organisations, petroleum and mining firms) can reclaim the sales tax they paid on purchases. Not refunded: tax on invoices from persons not registered for sales tax, on goods and services for the registered person's private use, on used goods exported, or still in dispute. No fee; gold-list members are refunded sooner (يسقط حق الم لف /المس ل في مطالبة المصلحة بالرد بعد مضي خمس سنوات)
note: The Tax Authority's refund guide, dated March 2024 (Ramadan 1445) on its cover; line 7 also shows 13/9/2022 without saying what it marks. It cites income tax law 17 of 2010 and sales tax law 19 of 2001. The text layer drops or replaces some letters (e.g. ئ for ض, ك dropped); quotes are as in the file.

condition: How a business receives a tax refund
state: By cheque from the account set aside for tax refunds, made out to the taxpayer and handed over through the one-stop window by registered mail or direct notice; or by set-off against other tax it owes; or, at its request, carried to a later tax period; the decision is sent by SMS, registered mail or direct notice (تحرير شيك من الحساب المخصص لالسترداد الضريبي لصالح الم لف/المس ل)

condition: Whether taxpayers can use the Tax Authority's services electronically
state: Yes, for refunds: a refund request and its attachments can be handed in at the one-stop window or through the approved e-services (أو عبر الخدمات االل ترونية المعتمدة)

condition: By when a business must file its sales-tax return
state: By the 21st of the following month, for the previous month's tax due (آخر موعد لتقديم المكلف إقراره عن الضريبة العامة على المبيعات هو يوم (21) من الشهر التالي)
place: Tax Authority in Sana'a's area (مصلحة الضرائب بصنعاء)
note: A one-line news item reporting the Tax Authority in Sana'a.

condition: What a small business must do to get a tax-exemption certificate
state: File its tax return for 2019 (or for 2020 if it started that year) at the tax office covering its activity or at the nearest post office, by 30 April 2022 as extended by Finance Minister decision 284 of 2021, to be given the certificate without fines; for small and micro enterprises with annual turnover up to 20 million rials, covered by the exemption in law 8 of 2020 (منحهم شهادة الاعفاء الضريبي دون احتساب أي غرامات)
note: An undated announcement on the Tax Authority's live site; it also covers small real-estate rent taxpayers (monthly rent up to 50,000 rials) and gives a free complaints number (line 27).

condition: What a small business must do to get a tax-exemption certificate
state: In 2023 the Tax Authority decided to renew exemptions automatically, issue them through its automated system every three years, and give them to small taxpayers free through the General Authority for Post and Postal Savings; it gave 74,040 certificates to small and micro enterprises from 1 February to 31 October 2023 (تجديد الإعفاءات تلقائيا واصدارها عبر النظام الآلي كل ثلاث سنوات ومنحها لصغار المكلفين مجانا)
note: A Saba report on the Tax Authority's site, quoting the head of the Authority.

condition: Whether taxpayers can use the Tax Authority's services electronically
state: Yes: from 30 May 2023 monthly wages-tax and sales-tax returns can be filed electronically through the Authority's site (e-tax.gov.ye); the tax number and tax card are already issued through its automated system (دشنت مصلحة الضرائب اليوم خدمة الإقرار الضريبي الإلكتروني الشهري)
note: A Saba report on the Tax Authority's site.

condition: Whether government taxes and fees can be paid electronically
state: Yes: income tax and sales tax, and the sales tax on qat, through the Tax Authority's electronic collection services (خدمة التحصيل الإلكتروني لضريبة الدخل والمبيعات)

condition: What zakat a business must pay on goods it holds for sale
state: A quarter of a tenth (2.5%) each lunar year on trade goods held for sale (land, property, crops, livestock and poultry included) and on industrial products, once they reach the nisab (the rial value of 85 g of 21-carat gold) and a year has passed; worked out by stocktaking and valuing the goods, adding cash, savings and collectable debts of the trade, less its debts and expenses; the shop, scales, calculating machine, ship and goods vehicles are not counted; property held for trade is assessed once, when sold (مقدار الزكاة في عروض التجارة والصناعة هو ربع العشر (2.5%))
note: Zakat law 2 of 1999, arts. 8 and 10, on the National Information Center's laws database; the page shows the 1999 text only. Art. 2 defines the Republic as the Republic of Yemen.

condition: What zakat certain service businesses must pay on their income
state: Private hospitals, dispensaries and clinics, manufacturing workshops, law, engineering and chartered-accountancy offices, and private schools, institutes and universities pay zakat on the year's income after costs, at the trade rate once the nisab is reached, deducted from the tax they owe (وعلى أن تخصم الزكاة من الضريبة المطلوبة منهم)
note: Zakat law 2 of 1999, art. 19.

condition: How a business must declare and pay zakat
state: File with the zakat authority (or its branches or the bodies it names) a declaration of the zakat due and pay that amount on time; pay from the goods themselves or in cash at their value when due; the payer may itself hand 25% of its zakat to the poor and needy; collections go into the authority's account at the central bank (أن يقدم إلى المصلحة أو فروعها أو الجهات التي تحددها إقراراً)
note: Zakat law 2 of 1999, arts. 27, 32, 42, 44; the authority is the Duties Authority (مصلحة الواجبات, art. 40).

condition: How a business must declare and pay zakat
state: To the General Zakat Authority: local authorities no longer have any power over collecting zakat, and the amended zakat law passed by the House on 4 May 2019, to be issued by the head of the Supreme Political Council, lets no other person or body collect or distribute zakat; some merchants have begun paying it to the authority voluntarily instead of distributing it themselves; Ramadan is the collection season (لا يجوز لأي شخص أو جهة غير الهيئة العامة للزكاة جمع وتحصيل وتوزيع وصرف الزكاة في الجمهورية)
place: General Zakat Authority's area (الهيئة العامة للزكاة)
note: An interview in al-Thawra with the General Zakat Authority's deputy for zakat resources; the rule on who may collect is his account of art. 41(c) of the amended law. He says the authority can't reach areas outside the Supreme Political Council's control (lines 60-61).

condition: Whether a business must pay zakat for past years
state: No, according to the General Zakat Authority, which calls untrue the reports that it demanded shop owners and businesses pay zakat retroactively for past years (بدفع فريضة الزكاة بأثر رجعي عن سنوات ماضية)
place: al-Mokha district and a number of liberated districts and areas (مديرية المخا وعدد من المديريات والمناطق المحررة)
note: A 26sep.net report of the authority's statement.

condition: What a merchant gets for coming forward to declare and pay zakat
state: Customs and tax privileges and exemptions, granted to merchants and large taxpayers who come forward to file their declarations and pay their zakat; the Zakat Authority and the Tax and Customs Authority are discussing how to implement them (الامتيازات والإعفاءات الجمركية والضريبية الممنوحة للتجار وكبار المكلفين المبادرين بتقديم إقراراتهم وإيتاء زكاتهم)
place: Zakat Authority in Sana'a's area (صنعاء: هيئة الزكاة)
note: A one-line news item; it doesn't say what the privileges and exemptions are.

condition: how many bank payment cards are in issue

condition: how many card terminals (POS) merchants have

note: Central Bank payments report, first half of 2025 (infographic).

condition: how many bank accounts exist

condition: which currencies can be withdrawn at ATMs
state: rials, US dollars and Saudi riyals: withdrawals given as 378,997 billion rials, 37,550 million dollars and 38,140 million Saudi riyals

condition: whether one may deal with unlicensed e-wallets
state: banned for all banks and exchange companies and establishments operating in the Republic, for 12 named entities, under penalty
note: The Central Bank's own news item (head office Aden, line 11), dated 2024-06-26; the list of 12 is in an attached document not captured here.

condition: how domestic money transfers can be made
state: new domestic cash transfers only through the unified money transfer network (UNMONEY); the local networks of banks and exchange companies stopped completely (bank networks allowed alongside it until 30 July 2024); all other cash transfers banned, except through licensed e-wallets and payment service providers within approved ceilings
note: Decision No. 23 of 2024 of the Governor of the Central Bank in Aden, issued Wednesday 26 June 2024; it addresses banks and exchange companies operating in the Republic (line 27).

condition: whether buyers can pay with a mobile e-wallet
state: available: more than 9 e-wallets, the unified transfer network and MEPS took part in a digital payment fair, with over 30 stores selling through digital payment
note: Fair held under the Central Bank's payment systems department; line 36: its stores sell only through digital wallets.

condition: how domestic money transfers can be made
state: through the unified network: 22 cash transfer networks cancelled and placed under one name; over YER 251 billion moved through it in 2024
note: Per the Central Bank's director general of payment systems, Kamal Al-Subaihi.

condition: who takes part in the unified money network (الشبكة الموحدة للأموال)
state: all banks and e-wallets have joined it
note: Per the Central Bank's director general of payment systems.

condition: which QR code standard financial institutions must use
state: a single, binding national QR code standard for all financial institutions operating in the Republic of Yemen
note: Decision of the board of the Central Bank, meeting in Aden on Sunday 29 March 2026 (line 25).

condition: whether money can move between different e-wallets
state: the Central Bank board approved linking e-wallets, to unify linking paths
note: Board decision of 29 March 2026.

condition: whether an instant (fast) payment system is available
state: the Central Bank approved taking a main stake in the fast payment system (FPS) operator company, with its executive to complete the steps
note: Board decision of 29 March 2026.

condition: whether rial banknotes are in short supply
state: a shortage of local-currency liquidity in the markets, despite the Central Bank's injections
note: Stated by the Central Bank board at its meeting of 29 March 2026.

condition: who takes part in the unified money network (الشبكة الموحدة للأموال)
state: restructured, with raised capital and the banks operating in the Republic of Yemen joining as shareholders
note: The Central Bank's own report of the company's extraordinary general assembly in Aden on Monday 27 July 2026 (line 25); a nine-member board of banks, shareholders and independents was elected (line 35).

condition: cost of shipping and insuring imports
state: rising transport and insurance costs and energy prices, with effects on supply chains, from developments in the region
note: As the Central Bank board reviewed them on 29 March 2026; the same sentence names the Yemeni economy among those under added pressure.

condition: whether one may deal in virtual assets or cryptocurrencies
state: banned, with their service providers too, by Central Bank circular No. 1 of 2026
note: Title in the Central Bank's own list of banking-supervision rules (head office Aden, line 67).

condition: whether customers can be identified electronically (eKYC)
state: yes, under Central Bank instructions regulating electronic know-your-customer procedures
note: Title in the Central Bank's list of supervision rules.

condition: whether mobile e-money services are regulated
state: yes: Central Bank instructions regulate mobile e-money services; Governor's decision No. 4 amends the e-payment provisions
note: Titles in the Central Bank's list of supervision rules.

condition: whether financial consumers are protected by rules
state: yes: Central Bank instructions on financial consumer protection (589, 20-8-2023)
note: Title in the Central Bank's list of supervision rules.

condition: whether banks must screen customers against international sanctions lists
state: yes: circular No. 4 of 2025 on enhanced due diligence and checking international sanctions lists
note: Title in the Central Bank's list of supervision rules.

condition: who sets interest rates on deposits
state: the Central Bank Governor, by decision No. 7 of 2026
note: Title in the Central Bank's list of supervision rules; the rates are not on the page.

condition: who may operate as an exchange company or remittance agent
state: those on the Central Bank's list of licensed exchange companies, establishments and remittance agents for 2026
note: Titles in the Central Bank's list; it also keeps a list of banks licensed in the Republic of Yemen (line 37). The lists themselves are not on the page.

condition: whether online stores can accept payments online
state: through Kuraimi Bank's E-Pay API: a supplier takes payments and reversals, which customers start from Kuraimi Bank's apps (KJ, Mfloos)
note: README of a third-party Node.js SDK for the API; its latest version is dated May 26, 2025 (line 198).

condition: what a merchant needs to take electronic payments through a bank
state: host a 'Verify Customer details' API that Kuraimi Bank calls, give the bank its URLs and Basic Authentication credentials, and hold supplier API credentials issued by Kuraimi Bank
note: Per the SDK README, citing section 13 of Kuraimi Bank's Supplier Integration Guide (line 29).

condition: which Yemeni banks are under US sanctions
state: Yemen Kuwait Bank for Trade and Investment, designated 17 January 2025 for supporting the Houthis: its US property blocked and US persons generally barred from dealing with it; wind-down allowed until 16 February 2025
note: OFAC designation under Executive Order 13224; items 68 and 69 are the same article captured twice.

condition: which banknotes merchants accept
state: old-edition notes only (الدفع بالعملة القديمة فقط)
note: The Dakhm online store's own payment page; it delivers with cash on delivery inside Sana'a (line 14).

condition: whether buyers can pay cash on delivery
state: available inside Sana'a (Dakhm store)
note: The store's own page.

condition: whether buyers can pay online sellers by bank transfer
state: yes: to the store's Al-Kuraimi 'Yemeni account' and 'Saudi account' (الحساب اليمني، الحساب السعودي) or its Haseb point
note: The Dakhm store's own payment page.

condition: whether buyers can pay with a mobile e-wallet
state: available: Jaib, Jawali or Cash, to the store's number
note: The Dakhm store's own payment page.

condition: whether buyers can pay online sellers by transfer through an exchange company
state: available: through Al-Hazmi, Al-Muheet, Al-Najm or Al-Imtiaz, to the named owner
note: The Dakhm store's own payment page.

condition: how buyers prove payment to online sellers
state: by sending a photo of the payment notice on WhatsApp
note: The Dakhm store's own payment page.

condition: whether parties pay for imports in cryptocurrency
state: a Houthi procurement network used Tron wallets, active since 2023 and transacting mostly in Tether's USDT (up to $1 million at a time), to buy commodities from Russia for shipment to Houthi-controlled Yemen
note: OFAC added eight such wallet addresses to its SDN list (line 960), barring U.S. persons from dealing with them.

condition: how remittances from abroad can reach Yemen
state: in stablecoins (USDC or USDT) through Digibank: converted in the app and paid out at over 1,000 liquidity points in Sana'a, Taiz and Aden, for fees of 0.5-2%, in one hour to one day
note: Digibank's own knowledge-base page, marked as edited 24 April 2025 (line 22); some steps on the page name Syrian pounds and the Sham Cash wallet (lines 142, 152, 158).

condition: fee for sending remittances to Yemen
state: 5-8% through traditional banks (3-15 days), 5-10% through Western Union (3-7 days), 5-12% through informal remittance offices (1-2 days)
note: Digibank's comparison table; it calls informal offices illegal with security risks, and says banks and Western Union are limited by sanctions.

condition: whether international money transfer companies pay out in Yemen
state: Western Union: yes, but limited to the cities by cash shortages and sanctions
note: Digibank's FAQ; the comparison table (line 185) says limited to the major cities.

condition: whether sending money to Yemen is lawful under US rules
state: personal or humanitarian transfers are allowed as long as the recipient is not on international sanctions lists
note: As Digibank's FAQ states the US Treasury rules.

condition: whether buyers rely on cash
state: most economic activity is conducted in cash, from day-to-day purchases to large-scale transactions
note: World Bank, Yemen Financial Sector Diagnostics, dated April 5, 2024 (line 42).

condition: whether one central bank and one currency serve the whole country
state: no: two central banks, in Aden (internationally recognized) and in Sana'a (Houthi-controlled), with inconsistent rules; two currencies in circulation, only one accepted across the country
note: World Bank, Yemen Financial Sector Diagnostics, dated April 5, 2024 (line 42).

condition: which central bank's rules banks follow
state: financial institutions with nationwide operations are subject to the authority of both central banks

condition: where formal banking services are available
state: largely restricted to major cities; rural and remote areas mainly served by money exchangers; 6.3% of adults have access to financial service points and there are 1.6 bank branches per 100,000 adults

condition: whether nonbank lenders are regulated
state: nonbank financial institutions provide credit but are regulated lightly if at all

condition: share of people with a bank account
state: almost entirely unbanked: about 90% of men and 99% of women; 4.8% of adults have deposits and 1.6% borrow from formal institutions
note: Footnote 2 gives the Central Bank of Yemen-Aden as source.

condition: whether depositors can draw their bank deposits
state: many banks froze some or all of their customers' deposits during the liquidity crisis
note: Same sentence: money exchangers let firms keep making international transfers for trade and households receive remittances.

condition: which rial banknotes may be used
state: transactions in notes minted after 2016 prohibited by the central bank in Sana'a
note: The source names only the authority.

condition: whether depositors can draw their bank deposits
state: commercial banks' deposits made before the central banks split remain frozen, and payments on domestic debt are suspended
note: Stated in the report's recommendation that these practices end.

condition: who provides payment services
state: mainly banks and money exchangers; the Yemen Post and Postal Savings Authority and the Postal Savings Fund also provide payment services and savings accounts
note: The sentence continues: 'services, savings accounts, and other financial products' (line 557). Insurance companies and pension funds play only a marginal role.

condition: who performs banking tasks
state: money exchangers: the primary destination for deposits and the main source of credit for traders, providing services such as trade financing once offered by banks
note: Lines 571-572: they serve a much larger share of the population than Yemeni banks.

condition: whether banks may deal in interest
state: a Houthi anti-usury law, in effect since early 2023 and partly implemented, makes banks switch interest-bearing accounts to checking accounts
note: The source names only the authority.

condition: who licenses and supervises banks and money exchangers
state: the Central Bank of Yemen in Aden, which also determines the exchange rate in consultation with the government
note: Under Law 14 of 2000 on the Central Bank (lines 905-911); most of the framework predates the conflict.

condition: which central bank's rules banks follow
state: both the central bank in Aden and the one in Sana'a supervise banks; banks headquartered in the Sana'a region report their financials to Aden, while the two banks' conflicting requirements persist

condition: whether financial consumers are protected by rules
state: the Central Bank in Aden issued a consumer protection regulation in 2023
note: Footnote 9.

condition: which laws govern banking and money exchange
state: Banking Law 38 of 1998; Islamic banks Law 21 of 1996 (amended by Law 16 of 2009); AML/CFT Law 1 of 2010 (amended by Law 17 of 2013); microfinance banks Law 15 of 2009; deposit insurance Law 21 of 2008; money exchange Law 19 of 1995 (amended by Law 15 of 1996); payment systems Law 40 of 2006; financing leases Law 11 of 2007

condition: how the central bank sells foreign currency
state: through a foreign exchange auction system introduced in November 2021, supplying foreign currency particularly for essential imports such as food and fuel
note: Introduced by the Central Bank in Aden.

condition: whether exchange companies may open accounts and take deposits
state: no: regulation prohibits any non-banking institution from accepting deposits; some large exchangers that took deposits are applying for banking licences
note: Lines 1145-1146: money exchangers are also subject to a new framework monitoring capital adequacy, liquidity and profitability.

condition: where merchants and households keep their savings
state: large money exchangers increasingly take deposits from the population
note: Same paragraph: currency outside banks rose from 44% of broad money in 2015 to 48% in 2022.

condition: whether banks and money exchangers must have audited financial statements
state: yes: the central bank in Aden requires financial statements audited by an independent auditor
note: Box 2.

condition: which rial banknotes may be used
state: notes printed by the Aden central bank after the 2016 split banned by the central bank in Sana'a: restrictions from 2017 (banks, exchange companies and traders barred from using them, sometimes confiscated), official ban from December 2019
note: The source calls the Houthis the De-Facto Authority, DFA (lines 473, 796), and places the ban's effects in DFA-controlled regions (line 1289).

condition: whether rial banknotes are in short supply
state: a liquidity shortage, as the pre-2016 notes in circulation deteriorate and cannot be replaced

condition: whether depositors can draw their bank deposits
state: withdrawals allowed on cash deposits made after September 2016; partly restricted on earlier deposits
note: Decision of the central bank in Aden; the source says the decisions of both central banks de facto froze most cash deposits made before the 2016 split (line 1428).

condition: whether depositors can draw their bank deposits
state: withdrawals allowed only on cash deposits accumulated since 2017
note: Decision of the central bank in Sana'a.

condition: what banks must do to keep access to international payments
state: implement SWIFT Scope, which the central bank in Aden mandated for all banks at the end of 2022; most major banks complied, with the Sana'a central bank's approval
note: Box 3; lines 1463-1465: banks that did not would have been cut off from the global financial system and trade finance.

condition: how the central bank sells foreign currency
state: weekly auctions, mainly funded from oil export revenue, in which banks bid volume and price for themselves or their clients; US$15 million a week at first, US$30 million from mid-2022
note: Weekly FX auctions run by the central bank in Aden since November 2021 (line 1707).

condition: how the central bank sells foreign currency
state: a US$2 billion line-of-credit facility funded by Saudi Arabia, giving banks and their clients hard currency to import five key commodities; banks had to deposit cash in Aden to use it
note: In use from 2018 to 2021 (Figure 16), then replaced by the FX auctions.

condition: whether rial cash may be moved between areas
state: physical transfers of pre-2016 rials to the south banned by the central bank in Sana'a
note: Stated as an obstacle for Sana'a banks to the line-of-credit facility.

condition: where formal banking services are available
state: access very limited, especially in rural and conflict-affected areas; people without access, or who distrust banks, rely on informal mechanisms

condition: what services banks mainly offer
state: foreign currency management, mainly money transfers for humanitarian actors and large private importers, and letters of credit, rather than lending and deposit-taking

condition: whether firms can get bank credit
state: very little: private credit fell from 9% of GDP in 2008 to 2% in 2021, and private-sector loans from 30% of bank loans in 2013 to 15% in 2020

condition: how many banks operate
state: 17 traditional banks (13 Yemeni, of which 3 state-owned and 10 private, and 4 foreign-owned) and 9 microfinance banks
note: As of the end of 2023; Table 2 (lines 2316-2351) lists them, source Central Bank of Yemen - Aden.

condition: who may obtain an exchange company licence
state: new licences limited where exchange shops are already concentrated, and minimum initial capital raised
note: Governor's decision No. 4 of 1444H of the central bank in Sana'a on initial capital (footnote 30); lines 2363-2364: the minimum initial capital was increased.

condition: whether banks may deal in interest
state: a law passed by the DFA legislature in March 2023 bans commercial and Islamic banks from lending at high interest rates; the source says it also bans murabaha; its application is ambiguous
note: DFA is the source's name for the Houthi de facto authority (line 796); the source names only the authority.

condition: whether authorities confiscate merchants' property and bank accounts
state: the Public Prosecutor's Office ordered Tadhamon Bank to seize 'VIP accounts'; when it refused, the DFA closed its head office for a time and confiscated its IT assets
note: Box 4; the bank's head office is in Sana'a.

condition: whether buyers can pay with a mobile e-wallet
state: available: Tadhamon Bank's e-wallet Mahfathati
note: Box 4.

condition: how remittances from abroad can reach Yemen
state: through bank payment networks such as Tadhamon Pay, used for domestic transfers and remittances from Saudi Arabia
note: Box 4.

condition: who provides payment services
state: money exchangers, whose networks blend formal and informal channels, carry domestic and international payments, including remittances and trade finance, for a fee
note: Lines 3395-3396: they earn revenue from transaction fees.

condition: whether banks can use the SWIFT network
state: CAC Bank's Sana'a branch was disconnected from SWIFT a few months after the bank's head office moved to Aden in October 2018, but kept serving DFA institutions and selected private clients
note: Box 4; line 3275-3276: the head office moved to Aden in October 2018.

condition: whether Yemeni banks have correspondent banking relationships
state: severely restricted, as Yemen's AML/CFT controls cannot be re-evaluated: listed by the FATF since 2010, with no on-site visit possible as of December 2023
note: Box 5.

condition: how many money exchangers operate
state: 96 companies, 233 institutions and 68 agencies registered with the central bank in Aden
note: Official figures as of 2023.

condition: how many money exchangers operate
state: over 170 companies registered with the central bank in Sana'a
note: Official figures as of 2023.

condition: whether the market exchange rate differs from the official rate
state: the market rate, shaped by money exchangers, can diverge significantly from the official rate set by the central bank in Aden
note: Lines 3400-3405: exchangers mainly convert currencies and give individuals and businesses access to cash.

condition: whether money can be moved between areas held by different parties
state: through money exchangers, as banks in the north and south are disconnected

condition: how many money exchangers operate
state: 415, up from 179 in 2014

condition: how many money exchangers operate
state: 91, up from 34 in 2014

condition: what a money exchanger may do under the exchange law
state: with the central bank's permission: buy and sell foreign currency, accept transfers from abroad, buy and sell travellers' and bank cheques, and other approved business; it may not take deposits or offer bank accounts
note: Article 14 of Republican Decree Law No. 19 of 1995, which governs exchange companies (line 3682).

condition: who may obtain an exchange company licence
state: minimum capital for a new exchange company raised, and new branches limited within a given area
note: Recent rules of the central bank in Aden.

condition: who may obtain an exchange company licence
state: regulations against the oversaturation of exchange companies and harmful financial schemes
note: Introduced in the first quarter of 2023.

condition: whether exchange shops are licensed
state: licensed exchange companies fell from 605 in 2014 to 550 in 2017, while about 800 unlicensed companies entered, often working under licensed ones as agents in tiered networks that reach isolated areas

condition: how domestic money transfers can be made
state: all money exchange companies and transfer networks must transfer through the Unified Money Network, set up after a resolution of the central bank in Aden of November 2020
note: Required from February 2024; lines 3727-3728: the network lets the central bank in Aden monitor transfers across north and south.

condition: what exchange companies must do with unclaimed transfers
state: report them to the central bank after two months
note: Box 7, after a list of unclaimed Emtiaz Express transfers leaked in early 2023; the central bank in Sana'a urged networks to build online tools to find transfers by name (lines 3778-3780).

condition: which Yemeni exchange companies are under US sanctions
state: Al-Omgy and Brother Exchanger (listed in 2016, alleged funnelling to AQAP) and Swaid & Sons Exchange (mid-2021, dealings with Iran)
note: US Treasury sanctions list, as the report states it.

condition: how much can be sent per transfer through money exchangers
state: from US$10 to over US$40,000 per transaction, with no limit on the number of transactions a client can make; importers and other businesses use these services instead of banks
note: Box 7.

condition: where importers obtain foreign currency
state: money exchangers, which became a credible alternative to banks for firms needing foreign exchange for trade
note: Same sentence: also for households to send and receive remittances.

condition: how remittances from abroad can reach Yemen
state: through banks, global transfer companies such as Western Union and MoneyGram (the second largest channel, US$1.1 billion inbound in 2022), and local hawala networks
note: Box 8; lines 4413-4414: their advantages are relatively low fees and extensive networks.

condition: currencies of transfers into Yemen through banks
state: mostly US dollars, then Saudi riyals, euros and UAE dirhams; US$4.9 billion in and US$5.6 billion out through banks in 2022
note: Box 8; data from the central bank in Aden.

condition: what money exchangers must report to the central bank
state: monthly data on capitalisation, leverage, profitability, liquidity, exposures and liabilities, used for a risk rating
note: The central bank in Aden's prudential risk-monitoring framework (line 5448).

condition: share of people with a bank account
state: about 8.8% of the population owned an account of any type, including an e-wallet or other digital account
note: From a 2022 study (SMEPS Digital Payments Study, footnote 48); account ownership was 3.7% in 2011 and 6.4% in 2014 (lines 5751-5752).

condition: whether firms can get bank credit
state: 9.5% of firms had a loan or line of credit in 2022 (5.3% in 2013); informal firms mostly borrow from informal sources such as friends, family or money lenders

condition: share of firms with a bank account

condition: whether goods may be traded between areas held by different parties

condition: which banknotes merchants accept

condition: whether Yemeni banks have correspondent banking relationships

condition: currency in which banks settle import payments

condition: where importers obtain foreign currency

condition: whether banks can draw their balances at the central bank

condition: how remittances from abroad can reach Yemen

condition: whether depositors can draw their bank deposits

note: In the Phase One section (2015 to 2019).

condition: how remittances from abroad can reach Yemen
state: through informal channels of the parallel market, which exploited restrictions imposed in Saudi Arabia on remittances from expatriates and investors, particularly limits on transferring large amounts directly

condition: how remittances from abroad can reach Yemen

condition: where importers obtain foreign currency

condition: how importers pay foreign suppliers

condition: whether electronic balances trade at par with cash

condition: how money transfers can be made

note: community-written project thejulan/yemenpay at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README)

condition: how a payment to a merchant through a wallet or bank payment API is authorised and completed
state: by the buyer's own transfer, verified automatically: an app on the merchant's phone captures the wallets' transfer SMS and bank-app notifications and sends them to be matched to the order; if automatic verification fails, the buyer sends a screenshot from the wallet app to the merchant to confirm the order manually (YemenPay)
note: community-written project thejulan/yemenpay at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README)

condition: what a buyer gives a merchant to start a payment through a wallet or bank payment API
state: the chosen wallet and the wallet's phone number (9 digits starting 77, 78, 73, 70 or 71), or for a Kuraimi account the sender's first name and surname (YemenPay checkout)
note: community-written project thejulan/yemenpay at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README)

condition: currencies a merchant can request payment in through a wallet or bank payment API
state: YER, SAR and USD; checkout offers only the wallets in which the merchant has an account in the chosen currency, otherwise it shows that no wallets are available for that currency (YemenPay)
note: community-written project thejulan/yemenpay at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README)

condition: what a merchant must hold to use a wallet or bank payment API
state: a YemenPay merchant ID and secret key, an active subscription (the pay button reads 'awaiting subscription renewal' when it has expired), and an Android phone running the YemenPay app with SMS or notification access, without which the app cannot work (YemenPay)
note: community-written project thejulan/yemenpay at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README)

condition: delivery destinations a merchant can offer buyers at checkout
state: a delivery city and detailed address taken at checkout when the merchant enables it, from the merchant's chosen list among 21 cities (Sana'a, Aden, Taiz, Ibb, Hodeidah, Hadhramaut and others) or all of them (YemenPay)
note: community-written project thejulan/yemenpay at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README); the 21 cities are listed in sdk/yemenpay.js lines 28-50

condition: wallet or bank payment gateways a merchant can call through an API
state: integrations listed for the AlQutaibiBank payment gateway, the Kuraimi Bank E-Pay API and SabaCash, in a directory offering payment integrations 'for a Yemeni or Gulf bank'
note: community directory yementechcollective/aweasome-yemeni-open-source at its latest commit (clients.tsv); not a provider's documentation (run README); its descriptions are 'taken from those repositories'

condition: who may provide payment services or operate payment systems
state: only a person holding a valid licence from the Central Bank; licensed banks may instead apply for the Central Bank's approval, and banks licensed for payment services before these instructions keep those services without new approval; exchange institutions may not apply unless they convert wholly into a payment service provider
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions regulating payment service providers and payment system operators, issued 13 September 2022 (17 Safar 1444); they apply to payment services 'in the Republic', defined as the Republic of Yemen; OCR text

condition: legal form and minimum capital of a payment service provider
state: a joint-stock company with paid-up capital of at least five hundred million Yemeni rials (seven hundred and fifty million for a payment system operator); the Central Bank may raise or lower the minimum
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: what electronic money must be issued against
state: pre-funded: issued against real pre-funded balances, after receipt of real cash in the currency approved by the Central Bank
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: services a licensed payment service provider may offer
state: among others: managing electronic transfers for electronic payments; managing the collection and/or payment of electronic funds; issuing and managing prepaid cards; managing international and domestic personal remittances; issuing and managing payment instruments other than debit instruments; issuing electronic money and executing the electronic payments it covers; other services the Central Bank approves
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: whether a payment service provider may run cross-border payment services
state: not without the Central Bank's written approval
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: what a financial service provider must tell customers about its fees
state: it must disclose and display its fees and charges, notify customers of them and of any change at least a month before they are imposed or changed, send the notice electronically, and display the schedule of fees and commissions prominently at its premises
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: what a payment service provider may not do
state: borrow without the Central Bank's prior written approval; accept deposits; extend credit facilities; deal in any way in virtual currencies; issue debit payment instruments
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: who bears a customer's losses when a payment or financial service fails, is breached or is defrauded
state: the payment service provider or system operator bears full responsibility, under its contracts and its responsibilities toward the services' beneficiaries, for faults, failures, breaches, leaks of information or mismanagement of accounts from clear and deliberate negligence, including the resulting losses
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: who may set ceilings on payment instruments
state: the Central Bank may impose restrictions on payment service providers, including setting ceilings for payment instruments, to keep the financial system stable
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: who may provide mobile e-money services
state: only a payment service provider licensed by the Central Bank to provide mobile e-money under these instructions, and a bank licensed by the Central Bank under circular 11 of 2014; a non-bank institution must first be licensed as a payment service provider
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: currencies in which mobile e-money may be held and transferred
state: the local currency (the Yemeni rial) only: issuers deal only in it, accounts open only in it, user-to-user transfers are in it only, and agents may not deal in any other currency; issuers may not offer currency exchange
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: limits on mobile e-money transactions and balances
state: individual accounts: 400,000 per transaction, 700,000 a day, 2,000,000 a month and 12,000,000 a year, counted cumulatively, and a balance of at most 2,000,000 rials; legal persons' accounts: limits set by the issuer with the Central Bank's prior written approval
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what a buyer must provide to open a mobile e-money account
state: a national identity card with the national number (or a passport) and a service activation form with at least full name, ID or passport number, date of birth, address and mobile number; a legal person, its commercial register; a mobile number registered with a local telecom company
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what identification a recipient without a mobile e-money account must show to collect a transfer
state: a national identity card with the national number, or a passport for foreigners, above 150,000 rials; at or below 150,000 rials, also an identity card without the national number, a family, military, social-security or voter card
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text; on line 322 the OCR reads '0 ريال' where the page image (page 07) shows 150,000

condition: how many mobile e-money accounts a customer may hold
state: no more than three accounts per customer in the service; each mobile number linked to one e-money account only, and each personal account to one mobile subscription with a network operator in the Republic
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: payments a buyer can make or receive through a wallet app
state: with mobile e-money: transfers to another e-money account, to and from a bank account, and to a person outside the service; paying utility bills (electricity, water, telephone); buying goods and services from merchants; receiving international remittances where these are received only through a commercial bank or remittance company; other services the Central Bank approves
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a wallet balance may earn interest or incentives
state: no: the e-money issuer may grant no interest or incentive on a user's balance
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a financial service provider may make exclusive arrangements with banks, telecom companies, agents or merchants
state: no: exclusivity is not allowed between the parties taking part in providing mobile e-money services
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what a wallet agent may do and who may be one
state: agents may open mobile-linked accounts, buy and sell e-money and answer customers' questions and complaints; ordinary agents may not sub-contract other agents, deal in a currency other than the local one, or charge the customer more than the contract sets; an agent must be a Yemeni national with an identity card, or a legal person with a commercial register
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: how a financial service provider must handle customer complaints
state: complaints must be processed within a reasonable time, none later than 10 working days from notification, and the consumer told of the right to refer unresolved complaints to the Central Bank
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what notice a wallet user gets of each transaction
state: an instant electronic notice (SMS or another channel) of each transaction made or received, showing the amount, the balance and the beneficiary's name
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what a financial service provider must tell customers about its fees
state: a mobile e-money issuer must notify users in writing or electronically of changes to fees and charges at least two weeks before they take effect, and tell the Central Bank 14 days before; the Central Bank may publish the fees and commissions issuers collect
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: who is responsible for transactions made through a wallet account
state: the customer who requested the service with identity documents is responsible for all transactions through the mobile e-money account, not the person using the phone
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: who bears a customer's losses when a payment or financial service fails, is breached or is defrauded
state: the mobile e-money issuer bears full responsibility for any failure that harms the customer, whether by the settlement bank, the telecom company or the agent, within the service provided, and must cover their liability by contract
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what electronic money must be issued against
state: mobile e-money is issued at a value equal to the funds received; the issuer may not hold the public's funds directly but must keep them in a pooled e-money (trust) account at a settlement bank, equal at all times to 100% of the outstanding e-money
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text; the page images show '100%' where the OCR reads '1100' (line 730, page 17) and 'لا يجوز' (may not) where the OCR reads 'Y -7 يجوز' (line 374, page 08)

condition: whether a wallet holder can redeem e-money for cash
state: yes: on the holder's request the issuer redeems e-money in cash at its equivalent value; issued e-money has no expiry date
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: how a financial service provider must handle customer complaints
state: answer every complaint with a decision within 10 working days of receiving it with all documents, extendable by 10 working days, and never beyond 30 working days; the consumer may take the complaint to the Central Bank within 14 days after the settlement period ends
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: what a financial service provider must tell customers about its fees
state: charge no fee not disclosed in advance; publish interest rates, fees and other charges at least every three months in Arabic and English in at least one widely read newspaper; show products, services and fees on its website and prominently at its premises; tell the Central Bank 5 working days before publishing; notify the consumer in writing, including electronically, before changing fees or interest
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text; the page image (page 24) reads 'كل ثلاثة أشهر على الأقل' where the OCR has 'كل BNE أشهر' (line 995)

condition: whether a financial service provider may make exclusive arrangements with banks, telecom companies, agents or merchants
state: no: a financial service provider may not take part in exclusive arrangements with agents and merchants
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a payment provider's system must work with other providers' systems
state: a financial service provider must use interoperable systems
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a payment provider's system must work with other providers' systems
state: a mobile e-money system must be ready and able to interoperate once an interoperability platform is available, at least supporting ISO 20022 or other messages the Central Bank adopts
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text; '15020022' in the OCR is ISO20022 on the page image (page 06)

condition: who bears a customer's losses when a payment or financial service fails, is breached or is defrauded
state: the financial service provider bears consumers' losses from fraud, embezzlement or misuse of the financial assets it or its agent holds and manages, and must return the money lost, unless the consumer's negligence or fraudulent conduct is proved to have caused it
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a customer may end a financial service or move it to another provider
state: yes: consumers are free to deal with any financial service provider; providers may not restrict ending agreements or switching to another provider, and must act on the consumer's request within 30 days of notice
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a buyer can open a bank or wallet account remotely, without visiting the provider
state: yes, for natural persons only: banks and providers licensed for mobile e-money may, with the Central Bank's prior written approval, onboard customers remotely by electronic know-your-customer with biometric identity checks; legal persons follow the regular procedure; exchange companies are not covered; for current and savings accounts the customer must also show an existing account at another licensed institution
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions regulating electronic know-your-customer procedures, dated 25 Rabi al-Akhir 1445 / 9 November 2023 (page image 16; the OCR of lines 665-666 garbles both dates); the scope names institutions, not an area; OCR text

condition: whether electronic records and signatures have the legal effect of written ones
state: yes, for records and signatures made in electronic customer onboarding or in providing financial or banking services, provided the requirements of the electronic payments and banking transactions law (no. 40 of 2006) and these instructions are met
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions regulating electronic know-your-customer procedures, dated 25 Rabi al-Akhir 1445 / 9 November 2023 (page image 16); the scope names institutions, not an area; OCR text

condition: which e-wallets and e-payment services banks and exchange companies may deal with
state: none that the Central Bank has not licensed: direct and indirect dealing is prohibited with the Cash, Al-Dawli Money, Jawali, Floosak, Saba Cash, Mobile Money, Yemen Wallet, E-Rial, Rial Mobile, Jaib, WeCash and Al-Mutakamila wallets, named as unlicensed, and with any other unlicensed e-wallet or service
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden, banking supervision sector: circular CBY/L/282/2024 to all banks and exchange companies; the page image shows 'Date:26/06/2024' and the heading '... العاملة في الجمهورية', which the OCR omits or truncates (lines 10-13); OCR text

condition: currencies in which mobile e-money may be held and transferred
state: the local currency and the major foreign currencies (US dollar, Saudi riyal, UAE dirham): accounts may be opened and transfers made in them; issuers may not convert local currency into any foreign currency
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: Governor's decision no. 4 of 2025 amending the mobile e-money instructions of 8/9 August 2023 (item 050), in force from its issue on 9 July 2025 (14 Muharram 1447); the decision names no area of its own; OCR text

condition: limits on mobile e-money transactions and balances
state: individual accounts in local currency: 1,000,000 rials per transaction, 2,000,000 a day, 5,000,000 a month, 50,000,000 a year, and a balance of at most 8,000,000 rials; in the major foreign currencies: 400, 500, 1,000 and 10,000 US dollars or equivalent, and a balance of at most 1,500 dollars; legal persons: set by the issuer with the Central Bank's prior written approval
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: Governor's decision no. 4 of 2025 amending the mobile e-money instructions of 8/9 August 2023 (item 050), in force from its issue on 9 July 2025 (14 Muharram 1447); the decision names no area of its own; OCR text; the figures are read from page image 2, the OCR of the table and of the balance cap being garbled (lines 74-94)

condition: what electronic money must be issued against
state: issued against receipt of funds of the same value in the local currency or in the major foreign currencies (US dollar, Saudi riyal, UAE dirham)
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: Governor's decision no. 4 of 2025 amending the mobile e-money instructions of 8/9 August 2023 (item 050), in force from its issue on 9 July 2025 (14 Muharram 1447); the decision names no area of its own; OCR text

condition: what a bank or exchange company must check before carrying out a customer's transaction
state: screen the customer and its beneficial owners against the UN Security Council, OFAC, EU, UK Treasury and local sanctions lists before and during any banking or commercial transaction, with specialised screening systems; refuse or stop dealings with any listed customer and report matches to the Financial Information Unit
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden, banking supervision sector: periodic circular no. 4 of 2025 to all banks and exchange companies operating in the Republic, dated 02/11/2025 (lines 11, 111); OCR text

condition: whether a financial service provider may deal in virtual assets or use them for payments
state: no: banks, exchange companies and payment service and e-wallet providers and operators in the Yemeni banking sector may not, directly or indirectly, for themselves, their customers or others, buy, sell, trade, exchange, transfer, move, hold or manage virtual assets, use virtual assets as a means of payment, transfer, settlement or meeting obligations through their products or services, or carry out, receive or facilitate transfers or payments made to buy, sell, trade or transfer virtual assets
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden, banking supervision sector: circular no. 1 of 2026 (Ref CBY/L/258/2026) prohibiting dealings in virtual assets, dated 15/09/2026 and in force from its issue (lines 237-239); its scope names the institutions under the Central Bank of Yemen's supervision, not an area; OCR text, checked against page image page-3.jpg, which reads كافة where the OCR has 48S, الأصول الافتراضية where it has Anal Addl, تسهيل where it has تسبيل, and الجهات where it has الجبات

condition: which exchange and remittance businesses are licensed to serve customers
state: for 2026: 100 exchange companies (partnerships), 231 individual exchange establishments and 111 remittance agents, each listed by trade name with its governorate and district
date_basis: range end (the list is of those licensed for the year 2026)
note: List of exchange companies and establishments and remittance agents licensed for 2026, a PDF on cby-ye.com; the document names no issuer and no area. condition: whether an exchange business may hold customer accounts or take deposits
state: no: whoever practises exchange may not open accounts for customers, accept deposits or carry out any function it is not licensed for under the relevant laws
date_basis: shown (the year in the list's title)
note: From the important notice at the end of the list of exchange businesses and remittance agents licensed for 2026, a PDF on cby-ye.com; the document names no issuer and no area. Checked against page image 10, which reads لا يحق لمن where the OCR has لابحق كن. OCR text

condition: what a remittance agent in a remote area may do for customers, and up to what amount
state: only work as the agent of a bank or a local money-transfer network to receive and send customers' money transfers, up to 2,000,000 Yemeni rials or the equivalent in foreign currencies per transaction and per customer per day
date_basis: shown (the year in the list's title)
note: From the important notice at the end of the list of exchange businesses and remittance agents licensed for 2026, a PDF on cby-ye.com; the document names no issuer and no area. Checked against page image 10, which reads لاستقبال وارسال الحوالات المالية للعملاء and مايعادلها من العملات الاجنبية للعملية وللعميل الواحد في اليوم الواحد. OCR text

condition: whether a merchant must be entered in the commercial register to trade
state: yes: trading in a shop is prohibited except to those entered in the commercial register of the area where the shop lies; individuals trading in a shop, commercial companies, public legal persons trading, cooperatives with commercial purposes and those running agencies or branches of foreign companies must be entered, an individual applying within sixty days of starting business or opening the shop; bodies dealing with merchants may not act on their trade transactions before confirming their entry or renewal; the Minister may exempt small traders he specifies
note: Minister of Industry and Trade decision no. 79 of 2019 issuing the executive regulation of Law no. 33 of 1991 on the commercial register; it cites the Supreme Political Council decision forming the National Salvation Government (lines 21-22) and defines the Republic as the Republic of Yemen (line 33); issued 17/4/1441 AH, 14/12/2019, and in force from its issue (article 30); the decision number, the year and the date are read from page images 01 and 16, which the OCR garbles; OCR text

condition: how long a merchant's commercial register entry lasts before it must be renewed
state: five calendar years; renewal must be applied for before the period ends, and an application in the following year is accepted with a fine of 25% of the renewal fee
note: Minister of Industry and Trade decision no. 79 of 2019, executive regulation of the commercial register law (article 5(d), article 16(a)); issued 14/12/2019 and in force from its issue; 'خمس سنوات ميلادية' and the 25% are read from page images 04 and 11, where the OCR reads 'خمس Ape Gl pie' and omits the percentage; OCR text

condition: whether a merchant must have a fixed place of business
state: yes: no one may act as a merchant without a fixed place in the Republic where they carry on their trade
note: Minister of Industry and Trade decision no. 79 of 2019, executive regulation of the commercial register law (article 23(2)); issued 14/12/2019 and in force from its issue; page image 15 ends the sentence with 'يباشر فيه مهنته', which the OCR garbles; OCR text

condition: what a merchant must show on its business correspondence and shopfront
state: its commercial register number and trade name, matching the commercial register
note: Minister of Industry and Trade decision no. 79 of 2019, executive regulation of the commercial register law (article 20); issued 14/12/2019 and in force from its issue; OCR text

condition: whether a merchant may let another person use its commercial register entry
state: no: the holder of a commercial register entry may not enable anyone else to make any use of it
note: Minister of Industry and Trade decision no. 79 of 2019, executive regulation of the commercial register law (article 23(3)); issued 14/12/2019 and in force from its issue; OCR text

condition: whether an agent selling a foreign company's products in Yemen must register the agency
state: yes: an agency is a contract by which a foreign company or house gives a company, establishment or shop founded or headquartered in the Republic the right to sell or distribute its products or carry out its business; the agent must be the foreign company's direct agent and must apply to the ministry to register the agency within sixty days of signing or certifying the agency contract, with a copy of its commercial register entry matching the agency
note: Republican decree no. 276 of 2000 issuing the executive regulation of Law no. 23 of 1997 on regulating agencies and branches of foreign companies and houses, signed by the President, the Prime Minister and the Minister of Supply and Trade; issued at the Presidency in Sana'a on 29 Jumada al-Thani 1421 AH, 27 September 2000, and in force from its issue (article 33); the decree number, the law number and the date are read from page images 02 and 20, which the OCR garbles; OCR text

condition: what an agent selling foreign vehicles, machinery or appliances must provide
state: for vehicles, agricultural and road machinery, equipment, electrical, electronic and mechanical appliances and any goods needing maintenance and spare parts: the goods must be unused, meet Yemeni or international standards and be supplied as the country needs; the agent must provide technical staff for maintenance, after-sales service with spare parts and modern maintenance workshops at the agency's head centre and the other main centres in the governorates, a workshop for each agency it holds, and train local staff
note: Republican decree no. 276 of 2000, executive regulation of the law on agencies and branches of foreign companies and houses (article 10); issued 27 September 2000 and in force from its issue; OCR text, checked against page image 07

condition: in which fields a foreign company may work in Yemen through its own branch
state: banking; technical and consulting services; private contracting and building roads, ports, airports, public utilities and housing; tourism and hotels; industrial investment; oil and minerals investment; agriculture, livestock and fisheries; other fields the Council of Ministers approves on the Minister's proposal; a branch working in the company's name needs a licence by the Minister's decision and must apply to be entered in the commercial register
note: Republican decree no. 276 of 2000, executive regulation of the law on agencies and branches of foreign companies and houses (articles 15, 16 and 24); issued 27 September 2000 and in force from its issue; page image 12 reads the first field as العمل المصرفي, which the OCR garbles; OCR text

condition: whether a merchant may import or sell American or Israeli goods
state: no: importing, exchanging or trading American or Israeli goods, or goods bearing American or Israeli trademarks, of any kind, is prohibited in the Republic of Yemen, including goods with an essential American or Israeli part; traders had at most three months from the decision to sell off American goods they held, Israeli goods had no grace period and are to be seized and destroyed, and American goods contracted for before the decision may enter and must be sold within three months of entry
note: Prime Minister's decision no. 10 of 1446 AH on boycotting American and Israeli goods, citing the Supreme Political Council President's decision forming the Government of Change and Construction (line 23), signed by the Prime Minister and the Minister of Economy, Industry and Investment; issued 20 Dhu al-Qa'dah 1446 AH, 18 May 2025, and in force from its issue (article 8); the number and the date are read from page images 1 and 2, which the OCR garbles; OCR text

condition: how a merchant pays commercial registration fees
state: the trade-name and commercial register fees and the publication charges are paid through the Mobile Money e-wallet (in the wallet app: Payments, then Government payments, then Government collection order, entering the collection number); the request is not sent for examination until they are paid; the commercial register fees of the ministry's office are then paid at that office against official receipts
place: Ministry of Economy, Industry and Investment (وزارة الاقتصاد والصناعة والاستثمار)'s area
note: Ministry of Economy, Industry and Investment, guide to applying for a trade name and commercial register for an individual establishment through its e-services portal, third edition, December 2025 (page image 03); the guide names no area, only the ministry and its offices in the governorates; the original PDF is not stored, its OCR and page images are; checked against page image 14; OCR text

condition: whether a merchant can apply for commercial registration online
